name: Manaslu & Tsum Valley
tagline: A quieter circuit round the world's eighth peak
meta_description: Manaslu and Tsum Valley treks: the Manaslu Circuit over Larkya La, Tsum Valley, Manaslu Base Camp, Larkya Peak and heli tours. Prices, seasons and permits.
summary: The Manaslu Circuit loops round Manaslu, 8,163 m, in 12–16 days from Kathmandu, climbing the Budhi Gandaki gorge to Samagaun at 3,530 m and crossing Larkya La at 5,106 m. The Tsum Valley is a 2–3 week Buddhist side valley. Best months are October–November and March–May; restricted area permits and a licensed guide are compulsory.
intro: Manaslu, at 8,163 m the eighth-highest mountain on earth, stands in Gorkha district between the Annapurnas and Ganesh Himal. The trek around it opened to foreigners only in 1991 and still requires a restricted area permit and a licensed guide, which keeps numbers far below the Annapurna Circuit next door. In 12–16 days from Kathmandu you follow the Budhi Gandaki from subtropical gorges at under 1,000 m to Tibetan Buddhist villages under the glaciers and over Larkya La at 5,106 m.

The circuit starts at Machha Khola, 8–9 hours by jeep from Kathmandu, and climbs through Jagat, Deng and Namrung, where Hindu and Gurung villages give way to the Nubri, a Tibetan Buddhist people. From Lho, Ribung Gompa frames the first full view of Manaslu. Samagaun, at 3,530 m, is the acclimatisation stop, with side trips to Birendra Tal, Pungyen Gompa and Manaslu Base Camp at about 4,800 m. Samdo, a day from the Tibet border, is the last village before the pass.

Larkya La is the hardest day: 8–10 hours from Dharamsala at about 4,460 m over the pass and down 1,500 m to the meadows of Bimthang at 3,590 m, facing Manaslu's west face, Himlung Himal and Annapurna II. The trail then drops through forest to Dharapani on the Annapurna Circuit, where jeeps return to Kathmandu or Pokhara. Climbers can add Larkya Peak at 6,249 m with an NMA permit.

East of the main trail, the Tsum Valley was closed to outsiders until 2008. Its people, the Tsumba, regard it as a beyul, a sacred hidden valley, and many villages have pledged not to kill animals. Mu Gompa at about 3,700 m, Rachen nunnery and Milarepa's cave are its landmarks. Lodges across the region are simpler than on Annapurna, with fewer attached bathrooms. Our packages include permits, licensed guides, porters, jeeps and teahouse meals, priced in INR and USD.
facts: Machha Khola (8–9 h by jeep from Kathmandu); exit Dharapani–Besisahar
Larkya La 5,106 m (Larkya Peak 6,249 m for climbers)
Manaslu and Tsum restricted area permits, MCAP, ACAP, licensed guide
Experienced trekkers, quiet trails, Tibetan Buddhist culture, heli tours

highlights.title: Crossing Larkya La at 5,106 m
highlights.text: The crossing starts from Dharamsala at 4–5 am, climbs about 650 m over moraine to the prayer flags and drops 1,500 m to Bimthang. From the top, Himlung Himal, Cheo Himal, Kang Guru and Annapurna II line the western horizon. It is a long, cold 8–10 hour day that needs acclimatisation.

highlights.title: Samagaun below Manaslu
highlights.text: Samagaun is a Nubri village of stone houses and barley fields at 3,530 m, with Manaslu's summit more than 4,600 m above the roofs. Rest-day hikes lead to the glacial lake of Birendra Tal in an hour, Pungyen Gompa in 3–4 hours return, or towards Manaslu Base Camp at about 4,800 m.

highlights.title: The Budhi Gandaki gorge
highlights.text: The lower trail threads the Budhi Gandaki gorge on cliff paths and long suspension bridges, past waterfalls, langur monkeys and terraced millet fields. Jagat's flagstone lanes mark the permit checkpoint. In three days from Machha Khola at 930 m, the valley climbs from subtropical forest to pine and rhododendron near Namrung at 2,630 m.

highlights.title: Tsum Valley, a sacred beyul
highlights.text: The Tsum Valley opened to foreigners in 2008 and remains one of the least visited Buddhist areas in Nepal. Walk through Chumling and Chhokangparo to Mu Gompa at about 3,700 m, visit Rachen nunnery and Milarepa's cave, and stay in villages that banned hunting and animal slaughter.

highlights.title: Ribung Gompa and Lho
highlights.text: Lho, at 3,180 m, has the most photographed view on the trek: Manaslu's twin summits rising behind the chortens of Ribung Gompa, a monastery home to young monks. Arrive by mid-afternoon from Namrung, then climb to the gompa for late light and again at dawn, when the mountain is usually clear.

highlights.title: Bimthang and Manaslu's west face
highlights.text: After the pass, Bimthang at 3,590 m opens onto a wide grassy basin beside the Bimthang Glacier, with the west face of Manaslu filling the view to the east. The next day's descent through pine, rhododendron and birch forest to Tilije and Dharapani is one of the most beautiful forest walks in Nepal.

getting_there: Most Manaslu and Tsum treks start at Machha Khola, about 160 km from Kathmandu. A private jeep takes 8–9 hours via the Prithvi Highway, Dhading Besi and Arughat, finishing on a rough dirt road up the Budhi Gandaki through Soti Khola; buses and shared jeeps take 9–11 hours with a change in Arughat. In the monsoon and after heavy rain the last stretch can be blocked, and treks may start walking from Soti Khola. At the end, jeeps run from Dharapani down the Marsyangdi valley to Besisahar in 3–4 hours, then 6–7 hours on paved roads to Kathmandu or 5–6 hours to Pokhara. Helicopters from Kathmandu reach Samagaun in about 60 minutes and are used for heli tours, trek-and-fly packages and evacuations.
permits: The Manaslu restricted area permit costs, as we understand 2026 rates, US$ 100 for the first seven days plus US$ 15 per day from September to November, and US$ 75 plus US$ 10 per day from December to August. The Tsum Valley permit is US$ 40 for seven days in autumn and US$ 30 in other months, plus US$ 7 per day. You also need the Manaslu Conservation Area permit and, for the Dharapani side, the Annapurna Conservation Area permit, each NPR 3,000 or NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals. Permits are issued only through registered agencies, and a licensed guide is compulsory; since March 2026 solo trekkers may apply. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Samagaun −12 to 4 °C, Machha Khola 7 to 20 °C, dry, snow higher up
months.summary: January is mid-winter in Nubri and Tsum. Larkya La is usually closed by snow, many families in Samagaun and Samdo move down to lower villages and several lodges shut. The lower Budhi Gandaki below Jagat is dry and pleasant for short walks, and the lower Tsum Valley stays open for hardy trekkers who want to see the Dhachyang horse festival. Heli tours to Samagaun still fly on clear mornings, giving sharp winter views of Manaslu.
months.tip: Choose a January heli tour rather than a trek if you want to see Manaslu in winter, as the pass is normally closed.

months.weather: Samagaun −10 to 6 °C, Jagat 8 to 21 °C, cold, late-winter storms
months.summary: February is still winter, with heavy snowfalls possible above 3,000 m and Larkya La closed in most years. Lodges higher up begin to reopen late in the month as families return. A lower trek to Namrung, or into the Tsum Valley as far as Chhokangparo, is possible with warm gear and flexible plans. Lhosar is celebrated in Tsum and Nubri in February or early March, with dances and family gatherings in the gompas.
months.tip: Check with your guide whether lodges above Namrung have reopened before booking a February trek.

months.weather: Samagaun −6 to 9 °C, Namrung 0 to 14 °C, warming, snow lingers on the pass
months.summary: March opens the spring season. Lower forests warm up and rhododendrons start to bloom around Namrung and Lho late in the month. Larkya La usually opens from mid to late March, but deep snow can remain and the descent to Bimthang is icy, so early-March crossings are uncertain. It is a good time for the Tsum Valley and for treks to Samagaun, with clear mornings and few other groups.
months.tip: Plan late-March departures for the Circuit, giving the Larkya La snow time to consolidate.

months.weather: Samagaun −2 to 13 °C, Dharamsala −8 to 5 °C, mild days, afternoon cloud
months.summary: April is the best spring month. Larkya La is normally open, rhododendron forests between Namrung and Lho and below Bimthang are in flower, and temperatures at Samagaun are mild by day. Mornings are clear, with cloud and occasional showers or snow flurries in the afternoon. It is the main season for Larkya Peak climbs, Manaslu Base Camp and combined Manaslu and Tsum treks.
months.tip: Cross Larkya La as early in the morning as your guide allows in April, before afternoon cloud and wind arrive.

months.weather: Samagaun 2 to 16 °C, Machha Khola 20 to 32 °C, warm, hazier
months.summary: May is warm at altitude and hot in the lower gorge, where the walk from Machha Khola to Jagat can reach 30 °C. The pass is usually clear of snow, and Bimthang's meadows turn green. Haze and pre-monsoon cloud increase through the month, so views of Manaslu are less reliable than in April. Late May brings the first monsoon showers and leeches on the lower trail. Treks should finish by the last week.
months.tip: Start the May walk through the lower gorge at dawn to avoid the hottest hours below 1,500 m.

months.weather: Machha Khola 22 to 32 °C, Samagaun 7 to 17 °C, monsoon rain from mid-June
months.summary: The monsoon reaches Gorkha in mid-June. The Budhi Gandaki gorge receives heavy rain, landslides damage the trail and the road to Machha Khola, and leeches are everywhere below 3,000 m. Upper Tsum and Samdo are drier, being partly in the rain shadow, but reaching them is difficult. We do not run regular Manaslu treks in June. Climbing expeditions prepare to fly in for the autumn season.
months.tip: Avoid June treks in the Budhi Gandaki, where landslides can cut the trail for days.

months.weather: Jagat 21 to 30 °C, Samagaun 8 to 17 °C, wettest month, cloud
months.summary: July is the wettest month. Rivers run high, side streams wash out bridges, and the road to Machha Khola is often closed. Mountain views are rare. Upper Tsum and the Nubri villages get far less rain than the lower gorge, and yak herders are up in the summer pastures, but the trek in is unpleasant and risky. Heli flights operate only in brief clear windows.
months.tip: If you must visit in July, consider a short heli tour on a clear morning instead of a trek.

months.weather: Jagat 21 to 30 °C, Samagaun 8 to 16 °C, heavy rain, clearer spells late
months.summary: August is still monsoon, with rain, landslides and leeches on the lower trail. Late in the month the first Manaslu expeditions fly to Samagaun, and the climbing season begins at base camp. Upper Tsum and Nubri are green, with barley ripening in the fields. Trekking is not advised, but the end of August starts the countdown to autumn as the rain eases in the high valleys.
months.tip: Keep two spare days in any late-August plan for road and trail damage after the monsoon.

months.weather: Samagaun 4 to 15 °C, Jagat 18 to 28 °C, rain easing, clearer late
months.summary: September is a shoulder month. Early in the month rain and leeches persist below Jagat and landslide repairs continue, but by mid to late September the skies clear and Larkya La is reliably open. Samagaun is busy with Manaslu expedition teams, who climb from late August to early October. Barley harvest is under way in the Nubri villages. Departures after 15 September usually get good conditions.
months.tip: Book departures from mid-September to avoid the last of the monsoon rain on the lower trail.

months.weather: Samagaun −3 to 13 °C, Dharamsala −10 to 4 °C, dry, very clear
months.summary: October is the peak month: dry, stable weather, crisp views of Manaslu from Lho and Samagaun and the best conditions on Larkya La. It is also the busiest time, though still quiet by Annapurna standards. Lodges at Dharamsala and Bimthang fill on some nights, and Dashain and Tihar holidays affect jeep availability. The Tsum Valley is clear and harvest-gold, ideal for the 20-day combined trek.
months.tip: Reserve October departures three to four months ahead, as limited lodge beds at Dharamsala fill quickly.

months.weather: Samagaun −7 to 10 °C, Bimthang −9 to 8 °C, dry, cold nights
months.summary: November is clear and colder, with fewer trekkers than October and very good visibility. Larkya La is usually open, but nights at Dharamsala fall to −12 °C or below, and a storm can bring snow to the pass, especially late in the month. Families in Samdo and Samagaun start preparing for winter. Bring warm gear, and keep a spare day in case the crossing has to wait for better weather.
months.tip: Carry microspikes in November for the frozen descent from Larkya La to Bimthang.

months.weather: Samagaun −11 to 6 °C, Machha Khola 9 to 22 °C, dry, clear, snow risk
months.summary: December is cold and dry, with clear skies but a real chance of snow closing Larkya La. Early-December crossings are often possible with a strong team and spare days; later in the month we recommend a trek to Samagaun and back, the Tsum Valley, or a heli tour. Many lodges higher up close by mid-month. In Tsum, the Dhachyang horse festival falls in December or January.
months.tip: Book a December Circuit only with two spare days and a plan to return via Samagaun if the pass is snowbound.

faqs.q: How many days is the Manaslu Circuit trek?
faqs.a: Usually 12–16 days from Kathmandu, including two drive days, about 9–11 walking days and an acclimatisation day at Samagaun, often with a second at Samdo. Our 12-day itinerary starts from ₹91,000 or US$ 1,050 and our 14-day version from ₹1,04,000 or US$ 1,190. Adding the Tsum Valley makes it about 20 days.

faqs.q: How much does the Manaslu Circuit trek cost?
faqs.a: Agency packages usually cost US$ 1,000–1,600. Ours start from about ₹91,000 or US$ 1,050 for 12 days and ₹1,04,000 or US$ 1,190 for 14 days, per person on twin sharing, including jeeps, permits, a licensed guide, porters, teahouses and three meals a day. Permit fees alone come to roughly US$ 170–200 per foreign trekker in autumn.

faqs.q: Is the Manaslu Circuit harder than the Annapurna Circuit?
faqs.a: Many trekkers find it slightly harder overall, even though Larkya La at 5,106 m is lower than Thorong La at 5,416 m. The pass day is 8–10 hours with a steep 1,500 m descent, lodges are simpler and there are fewer roads to cut walking short. Previous trekking experience above 4,000 m helps.

faqs.q: Can I trek Manaslu without a guide?
faqs.a: No. Manaslu is a restricted area, and the permit is issued only through a registered agency with a licensed guide who stays with you throughout. Since March 2026, as we understand it, solo trekkers can obtain the permit without a second person, but independent trekking remains prohibited. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time for the Manaslu trek?
faqs.a: October and November give the clearest skies and most reliable conditions on Larkya La. April and early May are the second season, with rhododendrons in flower. March and December are possible but snow can close the pass. January, February and the monsoon months from June to August are not recommended for the full circuit.

faqs.q: How do I get to Machha Khola from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: By road, about 160 km. A private jeep takes 8–9 hours via the Prithvi Highway, Dhading Besi and Arughat, with the final stretch on a rough dirt road up the Budhi Gandaki. Local buses and shared jeeps take 9–11 hours with a change. Our packages include a private jeep from your Kathmandu hotel.

faqs.q: Is the Tsum Valley trek worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, for travellers interested in Tibetan Buddhist culture and quiet trails. The valley opened only in 2008, has few lodges and stays below about 3,700 m at Mu Gompa, so altitude risk is moderate. Our 14-day Tsum Valley trek starts from ₹1,09,000 or US$ 1,250, and the 20-day Manaslu and Tsum combination from ₹1,56,000 or US$ 1,790.

faqs.q: Is there a Manaslu helicopter tour from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes. Our 1-day heli tour flies about an hour each way along the Budhi Gandaki, lands at Samagaun and flies close to Manaslu, from ₹1,26,000 or US$ 1,450 per seat. Flights run in clear morning weather only. People with heart or lung disease and pregnant women should not fly to high altitude.

faqs.q: Can Indians do the Manaslu Circuit trek?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian nationals need a passport for the restricted area permit, which as we understand it is charged at the same rate as for other foreigners, plus the conservation area permits at the SAARC rate of NPR 1,000 each. A licensed guide is compulsory. Our packages are priced in INR and include all permits.
